## Summary

Authored and persisted a 4-Story plan for the epic-scope task management platform. Gate #1 (intent) and Gate #2 (persist review) auto-proceeded under headless `--yes`; both plan critics returned `dispatch: false` (draft ≤5 stories, no risk/external-dependency triggers).

**Stories** (cohort `plan-run::f6c489b4`, delivered linearly via `depends_on`):

| # | Slug | Unit | Depends on |
|---|------|------|-----------|
| 1 | `store-and-migrations` | Store schema SSOT + idempotent `npm run migrate` (built-in `node:sqlite`, on-disk) | — |
| 2 | `rest-api-server` | `node:http` JSON API — auth/bearer, owner-scoped projects & tasks (paginated + `done` filter), async export enqueue; migrates on boot | #1 |
| 3 | `report-worker` | Background worker draining export jobs + unified `npm start` (API + worker) | #1, #2 |
| 4 | `admin-cli` | `npm run admin -- stats` / `deactivate-user` | #1, #2, #3 |

**Design decisions:**
- **Split past default-single** — the four units sit across the policy's carve-out seams (schema-SSOT/migration vs. consumers; separate deployable entry points), with Unit 1 as the sole owner of DDL and the others importing it.
- **Zero external dependencies** — `node:sqlite` and `node:http` are built-ins, satisfying "no external web framework" while keeping the store on-disk/persistent.
- **Soft-finding fixes applied** — specified pagination defaults (`page=1`, `pageSize=20`) inline, and serialized the two `package.json` writers (added `report-worker` → `admin-cli` edge) to clear the shared-editor conflict.
- **Accepted advisories** — the "thin dependent slice" merge suggestions were declined; low token estimates reflect lean specs, not thin work, and each unit is a real independently-verifiable deployable.

Ready for delivery with `/deliver 1 2 3 4` in a subsequent session.

Delivery complete. All four Stories of the epic landed on `main` via their own PRs, each `agent::done`.

## `/deliver 1 2 3 4 --yes` — summary

**Shape read:** ids (four Stories) with runner-set `--yes` (headless). The dependency graph resolved from live state as a strict linear chain 1 → 2 → 3 → 4, so each Story dispatched one wave at a time, building on the prior merge.

| Story | Unit | PR | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| #1 | Shared on-disk SQLite store + idempotent migration runner | [#5](https://github.com/dsj1984/bench-sbx-2026-07-25-epic-scope-mandrel-72e6c7d1/pull/5) | landed · `agent::done` |
| #2 | JSON REST API server (auth, projects, tasks, export enqueue) | [#6](https://github.com/dsj1984/bench-sbx-2026-07-25-epic-scope-mandrel-72e6c7d1/pull/6) | landed · `agent::done` |
| #3 | Background report worker + unified `npm start` | [#7](https://github.com/dsj1984/bench-sbx-2026-07-25-epic-scope-mandrel-72e6c7d1/pull/7) | landed · `agent::done` |
| #4 | Operator admin CLI (`stats`, `deactivate-user`) | [#8](https://github.com/dsj1984/bench-sbx-2026-07-25-epic-scope-mandrel-72e6c7d1/pull/8) | landed · `agent::done` |

Every Story ran the full engine — `story-<id>` branch → close gates (validation, base-sync, code-review all passed) → squash PR → merge to `main`. Each returned a `landed` terminal envelope. The per-run epilogue's sibling-coherence check across all four specs found no drift; its audit roster (clean-code, architecture, security, sre, dependencies, performance, quality) is advisory follow-up, not part of this delivery.

The 28-file platform is on `main`: store + migrations, `node:http` REST API applying migrations on boot, background worker with `npm start` supervisor, and the admin CLI — with `migrate`, `start`, and `admin` npm scripts wired up.

Note: each Story's local base fast-forward was reported skipped (`dirty-tree`, from the lingering worktree dirs) — a cosmetic tail degradation, not a landing issue; I fast-forwarded local `main` between waves so each Story branched from the correct base, and it now matches `origin/main`.
